title: Preferences
summary: How the user wants study material presented in this project (visual, step-by-step over prose); read before building or revising any deliverable here
details: Prose reading doesn't attract them; wants chemistry shown "as if you took it all apart", drawn by parts (atom → bonds → electrons → arrows) like their own handwritten notes, with the why of each arrow/electron movement explained, and wants to study through exercises supported by the theory.

Menu and buttons stopped working in their viewer at one point (fixed by making them JS-free), but in earlier versions they could rotate the 3D molecule viewer with their finger — wants that finger-drag 3D viewer to keep working; deliverables should also work without JS.

For hybridization/structure exercises: draw the full developed molecule (all H, bonds, lone pairs, charges) and write the hybridization (sp³/sp²/sp) ABOVE each atom with its why, part by part — the format they liked for U1/U2.

Wants each guide exercise shown as the original statement (cut from the PDF) with its step-by-step resolution directly underneath, then the next exercise; theory texts belong in the theory part, not among exercises; exercises should be reachable per unit.

Always develop the molecules: every analysis (not just hybridization) must be done on the drawn, developed molecule — "es todo el análisis literal que se necesita en química orgánica"; no text-only answers.

Reading colors: found the light/warm-paper version "muy blanco"; prefers the dark navy-blue reading theme (like the original interactive-guide sections) for concentration (previously asked for warm paper, then switched to dark blue).

Authorized searching the internet to verify their bibliography when a project source is unreadable (e.g. Wade), and to build figures from scratch instead; wants duplicated material unified whenever that is better for studying.

Don't remove or change anything they didn't ask for (it happened once with the 3D viewer); apply corrections only when sure they're right, and when asked whether something is correct, check online and defend the answer with cited sources.

When they get confused on a point, wants it written into that exercise as a "¡OJO! / cuidado, no confundir" box placed directly under that inciso's resolution, to study from; wants ring carbons numbered (C1, C2…) with angles marked, and every molecule the statement mentions drawn.

For class material they send (board drawings, class transcripts, cátedra guides): everything goes into the theory, nothing omitted ("me toman todo") — wants the full class wording included word for word, ordered by topic, and redrawn boards carrying exactly what the teacher writes, verbatim; prefers a plan of where each piece goes and a self-check for anything missing ("calidad, no menos tiempo").
Doesn't follow internal video numbering ("video 90 o 91 no entiendo"): refer to class videos by their YouTube title (e.g. «Hidratos de carbono (parte 1/parte 2)») plus the minute.
Wants explanations pitched so a secondary-school teenager could follow them: very visual, with arrows showing what happens step by step.

Arrows in mechanism drawings must never overlap molecules/letters; preferred style: circle around the moving electron pair (or bond) to "select" it and send the arrow out from that circle to its destination.

Source/book notes must never be summarized — keep them word for word ("tal cual") or add detail; visual summaries are welcome only as an addition, and the full note text should stay open/visible while reading, not folded away.

When a board/photo drawing can't be understood, don't guess: send back the redrawn drawing incomplete (unclear parts marked) so they can complete it; wants lab (TP) material ordered theory → exercise, not as transcribed prose.

Never paste their own photos (lab or board photos) into the reading — original crops are only for guide exercise statements and guide theory; their photos must be replaced by clean redrawn images. Each lab TP lives on its own page inside the HTML (reached from «Ejercicios»), not on the Inicio/home page, so things don't get mixed.

Lab practicals (TP1, TP2…) go in the «Ejercicios» section with theory and exercises together (not in a separate theory part); wants them fully graphed: photos/images recreated as clean drawings, the experiment's dynamics shown (what is obtained at each step), and molecules built step by step with arrows like the guide-exercise boards ("me encantó").

Lab TPs must be organized by the student's reasoning, not by source: what we want → problem → minimum theory → what goes in → each step (what we do / why / what happens / visual right there) → what we observe vs. what it means molecularly → what we obtain → how it can be asked in an exam. Transcripts, original photos, board photos and older versions stay preserved but folded in a secondary "sources/audit" layer; real lab-object photos go exactly where they serve as evidence, not in a generic photo block. Reserve the word "Laboratorio" for the real TPs. Validate one activity as a pattern before applying it to the rest.

Study layer must read like a book: no editorial/design notes addressed to the student, source citations as small discreet markers (full trace kept in audit), literal source text used to write a clean faithful formulation with the literal version folded behind «▶ Ver formulación literal», EXACT vs LECTURA_PROBABLE never given the same visual weight, and source quotes kept as quotes but not used as the canonical physical/chemical explanation (preserving a phrase ≠ recommending/teaching it).

The "original" is the single HTML with theory and exercises; new or redone material (e.g. TP1/TP2) replaces the old version inside it, not as separate files. Wants each thing opened from the menu (a unit's theory, a unit's exercises, each TP) to show as its own independent page, not appear inside a long page that already has earlier content ("queda feo de leer"). Chapters are NOT one per page: all of a unit's chapters stay together in that unit's theory page — the point is only not to mix theory with exercises.

Always search the internet whenever the project sources don't give the why of something ("vos tenés que siempre buscar internet") — they can't invent a fundamento if asked in an exam; act as a chemistry professor/researcher. In lab step-by-steps, every step from having the materials to obtaining the result must be shown graphically: what to do, what each thing/lab element is, what is used, how much, where it comes from, and why.
After content has been moved between pages, wants an ultra-exhaustive check that everything is where it belongs and nothing was left behind.

For studying TP1/TP2 wants each consigna/inciso shown separately with everything that answers it directly underneath, then the next inciso — very detailed but not overloaded ("me pierdo un poco" otherwise).

Curved electron-movement arrows must run parallel to the molecule's skeleton (from the moving pair/bond to its destination), never arching toward the centre of a ring — otherwise it reads as electrons going to the centre; approved as the rule for U2 exercise 8 onward. A curved arrow must not touch/rest on a bond either: flip it to arch on the free side. When a resolution has several arrows, wants each arrow shown step by step and told which ones happen simultaneously ("me pierdo" otherwise). Finds working out the final state/charges after moving electrons hard: wants a simple rule "en criollo" that always works.

When a concept question comes up while reviewing an exercise (e.g. "¿para qué es un radical?"), wants the answer added both as a short box in that exercise and as an ultra-detailed theory section built from the project's own sources — written like a "profe piola" of organic chemistry: easy to understand, concise, not generic.

In electron-movement drawings: the electrons that move must be shown in colour, and in the result whatever arrived (new bond line, new lone pair) must be drawn on the same side the arrow pointed to — otherwise the arrow seems to indicate the wrong line/pair. Wants bond-breaking shown with more intermediate steps and more indications. When the before/after look alike or a molecule is crowded, liked the enlarged "zoom" step-by-step view, keeping the original side-by-side view above it.
Whenever a molecule drawing is changed, the guided answer text beside it (the step-by-step on the right) must be updated to match the new drawing.

Each exercise resolution should start with a «DATOS» section drawing the molecules the statement names (hydrogens drawn, not just a zigzag skeleton), then a «PROCESO» section with the rest; loved the "lupa" frames showing electrons as dots step by step ("eso quería, entender paso a paso"); dotted lines must not overlap, no big empty space under the drawing, and concepts used (e.g. London) should link to the theory.

In multiple-choice exercises, each option must be developed on its own: which molecules it names and why it is or isn't true for each one ("por qué sí / por qué no"), not just the final answer. In every view of a molecule (not only the first) carbons stay numbered, charges/polar zones are enclosed ("englobar"), dipole vectors must not overlap labels or subscripts, and the developed drawing comes with its molecular formula.

For resolving exercises, base the how and why of every process and drawing on his own sources first (the project's files and what was worked out in the other chemistry chats); asked to remember that the class videos are on YouTube and count among those sources.
